name: Florida
summary: A red saltire on white with the state seal in the centre: a Seminole woman scattering flowers, a sabal palm, a steamboat and a rising sun. The red saltire was added in 1900.
origin: From 1868 Florida's flag was the seal on a white field. Governor Francis P. Fleming proposed adding the red saltire so the flag would not look like a white flag of surrender; voters approved it in 1900.
The seal was revised in 1985, correcting the woman's dress to Seminole style and replacing a cocoa tree with a sabal palm.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The saltire; no meaning set in law.

symbols.name: Sabal palm
symbols.description: The state tree, beside the woman.

symbols.name: Steamboat and sun
symbols.description: A steamboat sailing under a rising sun.
symbols.meaning: Commerce and the 'Sunshine State'; the motto 'In God We Trust'.

facts: The saltire was partly added so the flag would not look like a flag of surrender when hanging limp.
Alabama's flag has the same saltire without the seal.
Florida was under Spanish, British and French flags before joining the US.
clues: A red saltire on white with a seal showing a woman, a palm and a steamboat.
Its saltire was added so it would not look like a surrender flag.
Its neighbour's flag is the same saltire without a seal.
